Glenn A Kelly was born in Maine, USA. His father was a career US Air Force pilot, and his mother an avid artist. Growing up as a military brat Glenn lived in Okinawa, Japan, and California as his father was transferred to different assignments.

Glenn attended San Diego State University where he received a Bachelor's in Telecommunications and Film. Desiring to serve his country he joined the US Army and served honorably for four years. Glenn worked at Microsoft Corporation in Washington for 12 years where he met his wife and started a family.

Glenn, his wife, and two children moved to California in 2015 to join DreamWorks Animation as a Technology Manager, realizing his childhood dream of working in the entertainment industry.

item.title: Top 10 influential albums growing up
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
Music is a gift from God that I have enjoyed all my life. My tastes have changed over the years and I enjoy listening to so many different types of music genres. I have also played the clarinet in band and orchestra and piano. I don't have a great voice but I do love to sing and worship the Lord as well. There is such a connection to my emotions when I sing or listen to music. This post focuses on the top 10 albums that influenced me growing up.

#1 - Star Wars

I must start with Maestro John Williams as he is so gifted that this whole list could be filled with his work. I saw Star Wars in 1977 when it came out. My sister took me to see it and I had no idea what the movie was supposed to be about. I was 11 years old and you can only imagine how much seeing that Movie and hearing the wonderful music had an impact on me. I went home and bought the album and would listen to it over and over. I probably played the album four times a day for a year. I knew every beat and could hear the London Symphony Orchestra players breath and bump their music stands, and even in one song I think I hear someone sigh. I absolutely love this album.

#2 - The Police - Synchronicity

I listened to this album over and over as a teenager and have enjoyed these songs my whole life. During a bible study greeting time my pastor asked as an ice breaker question if we could be like any singer/musical performer in history who would we be. It was a hard question but I chose Sting as he has had such an amazing career and is still going strong. All of the members of The Police are gifted and talented.

#3 - Michael Jackson - Thriller

This album came out in 1982 when I was in High School and for me evokes so many great memories. Not everyone was or is a fan of Michael Jackson today. But for me his music and music videos made me want to dance, and had such an energy and spirit that spoke to me. His concerts were so popular I never was able to see him perform in person but I would have loved to have seen him in concert where his showmanship and flair was truly innovative and magical.

#4 - Wagner: Tannhauser

My father introduced me to classical music when I was young, he loved Sergey Rachmaninov who was an amazing pianist. Within Classical music the Romantic Period is my favorite and Richard Wagner is my favorite composer from that period. And if I had to pick one work of Wagner it would be Tannhauser. Many would pick The Ring as his crowning achievement but for me the passion and drama in Tannhauser are unparalleled. If you can’t handle opera singing (which for me was an acquired taste) then there are versions of Tannhauser Without Words that just features the beautiful music. When you listen to it you will see where many film composers get their inspiration.

#5 - The Doors - The Best Of The Doors

When it comes to American Rock and Roll one of my favorites is The Doors. I had heard their music growing up and it really got a hold of me when the movie The Doors came out and I started listening to all of their music. This album is a Best of compilation that has many of their greatest hits.

#6 - Earth, Wind & Fire - Greatest Hits

I loved the music from this band growing up and they have an impact and influence even to this day with their innovative style. It is hard to nail down their style but I found one online source that said they were a pop, soul, and jazz-fusion band. I can’t help but start to move and groove when I hear their tunes.

#7 - Madonna - The Immaculate Collection

I was a big Madonna fan growing up and saw her in concert a couple times which was quite an experience. The Who’s That Girl World Tour at Anaheim Stadium was the first Madonna concert I had been to and when she beckoned the fans forward I was able to get to the first and second row of seats where we were all standing on the seats and smashed together and screaming and dancing away. I do not follow her more recent work but it definitely made an impression on me growing up.

#8 - David Foster - Love Lights The World

David Foster’s career is still going strong from the 1970’s to this day. He is a phenomenal producer, composer, and arranger. He has worked with so many artists and is known in the music industry as the Hit Man as he has had so much success in producing hit songs. It is hard to pick just one album but for me my very favorite song is track 4 on this album entitled - Listen to the children. It is a sweet and gentle piano piece that I love.

#9 - Janet Jackson's - Rhythm Nation 1814

I was a big Janet Jackson fan growing up as her music had such energy. This was a memorable album for me as I saw Janet in concert at the Forum in Los Angeles. What a performance! So much energy. I do not follow her more recent works but still listen to her old songs with fondness.

#10 - The Best of Bond... James Bond

There is no way that I could complete a top ten album list without featuring music from James Bond. The theme songs and the movie soundtracks are an enduring favorite for me. I even like to listen to the soundtrack with all the dialogue and sound effects. I’m a bit strange that way. In particular Time To Get Out from Quantum of Solace is a favorite (opening car chase scene).

What music influenced you growing up?

I love so many different types of music. I have playlists for music that I listened to when I was growing up, for working out, for when I want to listen to worship music, dance music, or soundtracks.

item.title: Prayer Warrior
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
The bible is clear that our lives are not merely a physical existance but rather includes an unseen spiritual realm where a battle is being waged between good and evil forces. Prayer is an essential discipline for a believer to grow in their relationship with the Lord. In this article we will journey from learning the basics about prayer to encouraging personal growth and maturity in expressing your faith through prayer.

Grammar Stage of Prayer: In the grammar stage, prayer is about learning the basic ‘language’ of prayer. This includes understanding the structure of prayers, the different types of prayers (such as praise, thanksgiving, confession, and intercession), and the appropriate times and contexts for each. It’s about memorizing prayers, understanding the words used, and the order in which they are said. It’s the stage where one learns the ‘rules’ of prayer.

Logic Stage of Prayer: In the logic stage, prayer becomes more about understanding and internalizing the principles and truths expressed in these prayers. It’s about reflecting on the meanings behind the words, connecting personal experiences with the themes of the prayers, and beginning to see the bigger picture of how individual prayers fit into the broader Christian narrative. It’s the stage where one begins to reason with the ‘rules’ learned in the grammar stage.

Rhetoric Stage of Prayer: In the rhetoric stage, prayer is about expressing these truths eloquently and persuasively in one’s own words. It’s about personalizing prayer, making it a genuine expression of one’s own faith, hopes, fears, and love. It’s about using prayer as a way to articulate personal faith and to connect with God on a deeper level. It’s the stage where one applies the ‘rules’ in a way that is both true to the tradition and authentic to oneself.

Who is supposed to pray?

We are all supposed to pray. In 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 it states "Rejoice always; pray without ceasing; in everything give thanks, for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus."

What is prayer?

Simple put prayer is communication with God. God wants a relationship with us.

When are you supposed to pray?

In the area of motivation the bible has a great deal to say. To start with God is incredibly interested in our motivations, the why behind what we do. The bible tells us that our motivation should not be for selfish gain or to seek the approval of men but rather our motivation should come from a desire to obey and honor God.

Where are you supposed to pray?

The following are key bible verses that are related to motivation. It is by no means exhaustive but gives you a starting point to learning more about what biblical motivation looks like.

How are you supposed to pray?

Matthew 6:5-14

5 “And when you pray, you are not to be like the hypocrites; for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, they have their reward in full. 6 But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees what is done in secret will reward you.

7 “And when you are praying, do not use meaningless repetition as the Gentiles do, for they suppose that they will be heard for their many words. 8 Therefore, do not be like them; for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

9 “Pray, then, in this way:

‘Our Father who is in heaven,
Hallowed be Your name.
10 Your kingdom come.
Your will be done,
On earth as it is in heaven.
11 Give us this day our daily bread.
12 And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
13 And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. [For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.’]"

Why are you supposed to pray?

Ephesians 6:10-18

Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the might of His strength. Put on the full armor of God, so that you will be able to stand firm against the schemes of the devil. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world forces of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. Therefore, take up the full armor of God, so that you will be able to resist in the evil day, and having done everything, to stand firm. Stand firm therefore, having girded your loins with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and having shod your feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace. In addition to all, having taken up the shield of faith with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one, also receive the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, praying at all times with all prayer and petition in the Spirit, and to this end, being on the alert with all perseverance and petition for all the saints,

item.title: In the beginning...
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
I was born during a winter snowstorm in Maine, USA, just in time for dinner. My father was an Air Force pilot from a small town in West Virginia and my mother was a delicate flower from Tokyo, Japan that was an avid artist.

What's in a name?

My parents named me Glenn Arthur Kelly. Each name had a special reason for why they were chosen.

My first name Glenn was for John Glenn the astronaut and Pastor William Glenn Harris that was my Father's Uncle.

My middle name Arthur was for King Arthur and General Douglas MacArthur.

Quite a name to live up to!

Earliest memories

One of my earliest memories comes from when I was a little over one year old and was in our house when we lived in Okinawa. I remember the house and playing outside.

When I was three to seven years old I lived in Japan as my dad was stationed there. I remember playing in the streets of Tokyo with the neighbor kids and my cousins. I remember school and how much from the very beginning I liked girls and wanted to protect them in the playground.

I would ride my bike and climb trees and catch bugs. I loved when my dad would come home from work in his flight suit and would throw a football and we would play catch together.

I was not raised with any specific religious teaching. In subsequent posts in the Faith section of the site I will explore different topics from my past that have influenced and continue to influence me today.

I am constantly a work in progress, trying to better myself in all aspects of my life. First and foremost I endeavor to serve the Lord Jesus Christ so that he is honored in my thoughts and actions.

Together with my wife, and two daughters we live in Los Angeles, California where we are members of a wonderful local church family @Oak Hill Bible Church where I serve in the Audio/Video ministry and answer the call whenever the Oak Hill Deacon Beacon is projected in the sky.

In 2015 I joined DreamWorks as a Technology Manager and currently work as a Program Manager in the Project Management Office (PMO) that reports to the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of the studio.

Taking advantage of the tuition reimbursement program at work I completed my Master's in Business Administration (MBA) from The Master's University (TMU) in December 2019.

In 2020 I renewed my focus on physical fitness and started working out consistently and watching what I eat. For fun I took a free online prep course for being a Certified Personal Trainer from College of the Canyons. I did not take the certification test as it is quite expensive but I definitely learned a lot from the course!

I'm currently developing a podcast that I hope will be a way to connect and communicate with people around the world and develop a community, a place to gather and share stories and be able to encourage one another.

As you will see one of the consistent themes in my life is that I'm constantly learning.

People sometimes call these dreams their "bucket list" but that is a morbid descriptor for activities that you are passionate about and are working towards making a reality. All my life I have dreamed of the great adventures I would go on and many of them by the grace of God I have been able to accomplish.

I start by making a plan and then go after it with everything I have. We all have dreams regardless of our age or situation. As long as your dreams are not against God's will and perfect plan for you there is hope. I know that I have seen in my life time and time again where the Lord has blessed my dream and it came true. item.title: Just like you Dad
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
When I was a kid there was so much that I wanted to do when I grew up. My father was a major influence on me and when I was growing up I wanted to be just like my dad.

I want to be a pilot like my father

Being the son of a United States Air Force Officer, living on military bases from as early as I can remember in Okinawa, Japan, and California I was around airplanes pretty much all my life. I looked up to my dad and wanted to be just like him. He would come home in his flight suit after flying different missions or working at the office. I would always show him respect and call him sir. He would joke and say don't call me sir, call me Major.

Whenever we would drive on or off the base people would salute my Dad as he was an officer and he would be given respect for his rank. Also being a pilot in the Air Force has to be one of the coolest jobs in the world. At least that was what I thought as a young boy.

My room had pictures of airplanes and I would make model airplanes and have them on display. I remember vividly one toy I had that was an aircraft carrier about 6 feet long that had a string that I would tie to a bed post and I could launch small plastic airplanes from the carrier and it would slide up the string and then pivot and come back down, and I could guide it back for a safe landing. I also had a cool helicopter game that ran on batteries and the helicopter was able to fly around in a circle as it was attached by a metal rod, but it could pick up little plastic cargo containers and you could drop them off. I would spend hours and hours playing with these and other flying toys inside and outside and think of the day that I would be able to fly a plane like my dad.

On I think my 9th birthday my dad took me to the control tower at Edwards Air Force base with my friends and we got to play around in there for awhile. item.title: Martial Arts
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
There are many benefits to studying martial arts including physical fitness, self confidence, and mental discipline. Martial arts are an important component of my life that I have devoted several years of practice and study to, and have benefited me in many ways.

What are the Martial Arts?

Martial arts are codified systems and traditions of combat practiced for a number of reasons such as self-defense; military and law enforcement applications; competition; physical, mental and spiritual development; and entertainment or the preservation of a nation's intangible cultural heritage.

Wikipedia definition

To me, ultimately, martial arts means honestly expressing yourself. Now, it is very difficult to do. It has always been very easy for me to put on a show and be cocky, and be flooded with a cocky feeling and feel pretty cool and all that. I can make all kinds of phoney things. Blinded by it. Or I can show some really fancy movement. But to experience oneself honestly, not lying to oneself, and to express myself honestly, now that is very hard to do.

Bruce Lee

Motivations to study

I have always been interested in understanding the martial arts. Perhaps this is inherently something that men are drawn to as they want to understand how to fight and to win.

My father and I would watch heavyweight boxing matches together including Muhammad Ali and Mike Tyson. We would study the moves in slow motion over and over as we were fascinated by the precision, timing, technique, and power.

A key motivation for me was to be able to learn how to defend myself well and to be able to protect the ones I love. As I am half Japanese I wanted to understand Japanese culture of which Bushido and Ninjitsu are prominent.

What forms have I studied

I have taken classes and have been formally trained in Judo (when I was little), Wrestling (in Junior High), Karate (Japan Karate Federation - Shito-Ryu Itosu-Kai during High School, achieved Brown Belt), Aikido (Steven Segal seminar), Fencing (college course), Military combat tactics (while in Army), Kendo (classes), and Police defensive tactics (Police Academy).

I have studied Bushido, Ninjistsu, Jeet Kune Do, and many martial arts philosophies.

Cool time that I was one with the force

In the Star Wars movies and stories there is the concept of "the force". There was one moment in a Karate Tournament when I was 17 years old where I was in sparring match and had won my way to the final round where I believe I experienced what that is like.

My opponent had just scored what would be the winning point on me but there was disagreement by the judges. In a sparring competition there are four corner judges and the referee that is standing and moving around. I had blocked my opponent's kick but it had not been seen by a couple of the judges. So there was a conference of the judges and they corrected the situation so we were back to being tied. The next point would win the match and time was running out. My father, sister, and brother in-law were in the stands cheering me on. I was intensely focused and when the referee had us bow and begin again I moved within the blink of an eye and hit my opponent three times in his face with perfect control and precision.

I scored the winning point and won the competition. It is hard to describe but there was not even thought but just action. There didn't seem to be any time at all but just perfect speed and control. The perfect expression of what I had hoped to achieve in that contest. Viewing it from the stands my father later told me that my eyes were like fire with concentration and that I moved so incredibly fast and that the strikes to my opponents face were like a machine gun in rapid succession.

How have Martial Arts benefited me in life?

In particular when I was growing up it gave me some skills and peace of mind that I would know how to protect myself. I was not the sort that went around picking fights but rather strove to be very aware of my surroundings and sought to avoid being in a situation where I would get harmed or killed.

When I was training hard in a particular martial art form it definitely was a great workout that improved cardio vascular endurance, coordination, speed, and flexibility.

When I was studying Karate for several years and working my way up the ranks there was also the consistent culture of helping the other members of the class that was particularly impactful to me. The more senior students would really invest in those that were of lower rank. Also as a senior student you would then lead the warm up or calisthenics or be asked to demonstrate a particular technique so it grew you as a leader within the class. Of course there were the occasional bullies or people that were just there to hurt people, but by and large it was an incredibly nurturing and caring community.

What is his story? Where did he come from? In short he is a fictional role playing character that I created back in High School.

Role Playing Games

Back in High School my close friends and I used to play all sorts of role playing games like Advanced Dungeons & Dragons, Top Secret, and Gamma Wars (a hybrid game that we made up together). For those unfamiliar with these types of games there is basically a game master who is the story teller that sets the game mission or campaign, making up the plot line, premise/setting, and portrays the non-player characters. The other participants create their unique characters and play the game as this character, making their choices of which way to go and what they want to do. I had very imaginative friends that were amazing story tellers who enjoyed being the game masters and I loved being the one playing the game slaying dragons, rescuing the damsel in distress, or saving the world/universe.

006 Character

I created 006 as a character for the role playing game Top Secret. Basically set in the modern world this role playing game allows players to become secret agents and go on missions. To start with you have to create your character. The character has attributes like Strength, Willpower, Courage, Charm, Intelligence, and Coordination.

006 was a British Secret Agent whose standout qualities were his charm, knowledge, and coordination. On his many Top Secret game missions he would partner up with 001 (played by my friend Jon) who excelled in Strength and Courage. 006 is not to be mixed up with the character from the movie Goldeneye. In the Top Secret game my character had the codename 006 as I didn't want to be mistaken as 007 but rather be his colleague.

I have so many fond memories playing various role playing games growing up with my friends. We had vivid imaginations and shared many laughs as we adventured together. You must understand that we did not have many video games growing up or Virtual Reality so had to make everything up in our minds.

item.title: Dare to read God's Word
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
My life is a testimony to the truth of God’s word. I was born in the state of Maine, USA to a Japanese mother and to my father who was a career Air Force officer. After several military relocations my dad retired and our family settled in sunny Southern California. In school growing up I was taught, and wholeheartedly accepted, that man’s words were truth. When I was a teenager I ventured to read the Bible on a dare from Christian friends. This dare began my journey toward accepting God’s word as the source of truth and receiving Christ as my savior.

My parents taught me to be an honest, hardworking, and productive man. I was not raised “religiously,” and our family did not attend church.

In the public school system I was taught evolution and that there was no God, accepting all of this as fact without question. Thankfully God had His perfect plan and put many Christian friends in my path while growing up. I would argue for hours with these friends about the meaning of life and the non-existence of God. They would respectfully provide their perspective, encourage me to read the Bible, and invite me to church. Once in a while I would humor them, but I was firmly entrenched in secular humanist thinking.

If you haven't read the Bible for yourself I dare you to.

Proving I had no fear of this fictional book filled with superstition and folklore, I read the entire Bible in a year. It was nothing like I thought it would be. I certainly didn’t understand everything in the Bible, but gradually God’s word was beginning to work within me and would be instrumental in the next adventure I undertook. I had always dreamed of being a valiant soldier who served his country, so I joined the US Army. During that time in my life, I began earnestly crying out to God for help as the situations I was in were pushing me to my limits.

I would pray to God “Keep me alive today,” and “Give me courage to face the challenges that this day will bring.”

I placed my trust in God and He kept me safe. Over the years I wanted to know more about who God was and longed to develop a deeper relationship with him. After serving in the US Army for four years, I went back home to be with my dad as he struggled through serious health issues. God was faithful to me during my Army experience and by His grace I was ready to take the next step.

I started attending Saddleback Church regularly and committed my life to Christ in the summer of 1997, making a public confession of my faith and commitment to Jesus Christ as my Lord and savior through baptism. Since then the Lord has blessed me in many ways. One of the immediate changes that I noticed was in my heart. Up to that point in my life I would characterize my personality as being like the Star Trek character, Mr. Spock, who felt no emotion and was ruled by logic. After committing myself to Christ, I felt things more deeply than ever before and had compassion for others.

I’m thankful that my life journey for truth and purpose didn’t end with following man’s words as truth, or reading the Bible and not understanding it, or just with one act of obedience years ago to accept the Lord as my savior and be baptized. My greatest joy now is the continual growth I experience daily in my relationship with the Lord. At home my wife and I encourage one another daily to live a life that glorifies the Lord and do all that we can to live out our lives as a testimony of the Lord to our two daughters. As members of a local body of believers we continue to grow in our understanding of the Lord through studying His word, praying for one another, and performing acts of service in our church family and local community. God’s word continues to be a guide in my life and will truly be the only thing that will remain and not pass away.

item.title: World Vision Experience
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
This post explores why I applied to work at World Vision, the experiences and relationships I developed while working there, and why I moved on.

Why World Vision?

Back in 2010 while I had been working at Microsoft in Redmond, Washington for over a decade I started feeling like I was only employee #11487 to the company I had dedicated so many years of my life to. I was facing re-org number six at the time. For those who don't know what a re-org is, it is something that happens at large corporations where the employees are laid off, and the ones who survive are often moved into different teams and organizations. The idea behind this is that it stimulates productivity and efficiency. What it always did for me was give me a bad feeling in the pit of my stomach.

I started looking at job opportunities outside of Microsoft that perhaps might better align with my life goals and dreams. I looked into what it would take to be a police officer (which I'll cover in a different post) and into Non Profit Organizations that were serving the Lord in demonstrable ways reaching out to the poor and suffering in the world. At a Casting Crowns concert our family was introduced to World Vision and signed up to sponsor a child in Africa.

I saw an opening at World Vision US (WVUS), in Federal Way, Washington as a technology director and went through the interview process and the final interview was with the CTO and Director of development. In the interview I shared my testimony and tried to understand better what the position was about and they were curious about how I would recommend they approach their technology strategy and organize their business. It ended up that I was not selected for that position.

I applied a second time in the summer of 2011 at WVUS for a Program Manager position in the Marketing, Internet Business Unit, Client Engagement Team and was accepted. It was a big culture shock going from Microsoft where I had my own office and managed international teams and massive budgets. I was given a cubicle in an open area with seven other people and my first task was to help develop an internet development guide for the organization to capture standards and best practices. The people were all so friendly and we went to chapel every Wednesday and the company was like one big family.

While at WVUS I helped to completely overhaul their internet site and worked with the Director of Mobile Technology to deliver an iOS child sponsorship app. After almost two years at WVUS I was asked to consider a position at World Vision International (WVI) from a WVUS colleague that had jumped ship to WVI and jumped at the opportunity.

The position I accepted at WVI was as a Global Solutions Manager, in the Digital Marketing team and my job allowed me to travel to many of the international World Vision offices to help them with their digital marketing solutions and strategies. These were amazingly rich times where I was able to serve alongside brothers and sisters in Christ who were so passionate to help the most vulnerable children in need around the world.

Moving on

I soon found out that re-orgs were not just a thing that happened in for profit corporations but also happened quite often at global non profit organizations. Shortly after joining the team we were re-orged under new management where I successfully made the cut and then our director left the organization and we were under a completely new management. There were continued efforts to try to cut budgets and move teams offshore to cheaper locales. In this instance it was to move the whole service organization to the Philippines.

I started my search again for something different and my sights were set to go back to my original dream of working in the entertainment industry. After several months of searching and prayer I accepted a job at DreamWorks Animation and our family was moving to California.

Do not be afraid to get on your knees and pray that the Lord open up new opportunities for you to serve Him and pursue your dreams with resolve and humility.

item.title: What's your fitness goal?
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
Growing up if you were like me you loved to play outside all day with your friends. It seemed like we had boundless energy and could never get enough of play. Even eating meals seemed like a burden or time wasted as the priority was on play, play, and more play!

I have always loved to work out and after finishing my Master's Degree I was able to clear enough time in my schedule to focus on fitness with renewed vigor. I took the following approach as I am a big dreamer at heart and also a meticulous organizer.

Dream Big

First off I want to encourage you to write down your dreams, goals, and motivations for fitness. At least for me the dreaming part was easy as I can envision where I would like to be. There are many sources of inspiration throughout history and in the present day. I liked how one online resource put it. Ask yourself is your fitness goal to be:

Warrior Fit

Greek God Fit

Super Hero Fit

Set Goals

My goals were to be healthy, physically fit, including endurance, strength, speed, and flexibility. I do not aspire to be a professional bodybuilder but just wanted to improve on all dimensions of fitness. Some may want to lose weight, or run a marathon, or get ready for an upcoming wedding or to get into shape to go to the beach. What are your goals?

List Out Motivators

I recommend that you list out your motivations and review them every so often to help you stick to the long term plan and journey towards improved fitness. As an example my top motivators are:

Start with Prayer

Put the Lord first and go to Him in prayer. Some things you might bring to the Lord in prayer:

  • Ask for His will to be done
  • That you have the right heart motivation to seek His glory
  • Ask for His strength
  • Ask for His endurance
  • Ask for His wisdom
  • Ask for His blessing

Research

Start doing your own independent research into fitness and documenting your learnings. For me this was simple and I started with a pad of paper but then moved to a Google Sheet where I started pulling together the basics. I asked friends who are into fitness for their insights and resources they used to plan out their workouts. As you can imagine there is a lot of information available and much of it conflicting. I encourage you to start wading through all of the information out there and zero in on the basics as well as start a list of the advanced areas and approaches that you want to dig into more.

Tracking Body Measurements & Workouts

Keep a log of your workout exercise repetitions and weights and on a regular basis measure your body weight (some do this daily and average it out weekly) and take key body measurements (monthly). Advanced tip: Start taking monthly progress photos to be able to see how you look over time.

Reassess & Adjust

We are all on a constant journey of assessment and adjustment as you find exercises and diet approaches that work well for you and some that do not. Always look for new ways to mix things up and keep your body guessing. The key is consistency and not being discouraged as the results take time. In particular as you get older be careful to not push yourself too hard but be patient.

What are your fitness goals? Start your Fitness Journey today!

item.title: Diet Ops
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
My kids tease me that I put the word Ops after everything. Ops is military slang for Operations. There is so much information, often conflicting, available today on what you should or should not eat, making it extremely difficult to navigate. I've studied this extensively, consulted with multiple experts, and tried many different approaches throughout my life and continue to learn what works or doesn't work for me.

Basic Terms & Concepts

In order to determine your personal Diet Ops you must first understand a few key terms and concepts.

  • Calorie - Form of energy measurement. Used for energy or stored.
  • Calorie Balance - Calories In (consumed) equal the calories Out (burned/used). Tissue weight will remain stable (the same).
  • Calorie Deficit - Consuming fewer calories than your body expends. ALWAYS results in weight loss.
  • Calorie Surplus - Eat more than you burn. Your body stores these extra calories and this ALWAYS results in weight gain.

Priority #1 - Determine your Calorie Balance

The simplest method is to use a scale and weigh your bodyweight a few times a week to see how it is trending. A best practice is to weigh yourself the same time every day typically first thing when you get up prior to eating your breakfast.

1-2 lbs per week = Ideal rate to gain or lose weight

Depending on your fitness goals you may be trying to lose, maintain, or gain weight. If your goal is to gain or lose weight, research indicates that 1-2 lbs per week is the ideal rate or pace to set to achieve your goals. A pound of tissue is composed of 3,500 calories. To build a pound of tissue, 3,500 calories must be consumed in excess of your calorie balance. To lose a pound, a deficit of 3,500 calories is required. So divide 3,500 calories by 7 days in a week and you get the following rule of thumb: Adjust 500 - 1,000 calories/day to achieve the best results.

Priority #2 - Dial in your Macronutrients

Macronutrients are a substance required in relatively large amounts for the normal growth and development of an organism. Macronutrients for animals include fat, carbohydrate, and protein.

Proteins are the most important dietary macronutrient as muscle is made out of it. Protein intake is essential to build new muscle and save your existing muscle. About 1g of protein per pound of body weight is best for most people.

The primary role of carbohydrates (carbs) is to provide energy for your workouts and for recovery. Higher carbs should be eaten with higher workout volumes and daily activity levels.

Healthy/essential fats in small amounts are required for survival as they are the basis for many hormones and chemical messengers in your body.

Priority #3 - Nutrient Timing

Nutrient timing is all about when/how frequently you take in your nutrients and its relationship to activity.

General principles

  • Eat healthy food sources that are fresh and not processed as much as possible.
  • Read the nutrient labels on foods carefully to see what all the ingredients that go into the product.
  • Be sensitive to how your body feels and responds to different foods and adjust your diet accordingly.
  • I know that I am allergic to some foods or ingredients and avoid them diligently as I know if I do not then I will suffer the consequences.
  • Drink plenty of water throughout the day as being hydrated is important to your overall health.

Eating healthy is a lifetime pursuit so do not be discouraged if your progress towards your goals is not happening at the pace you want it to.

Brethren, I do not regard myself as having laid hold of it yet; but one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.

After you have determined your fitness goal (covered in the post - What's your fitness goal?) these are good basics to begin to make your personal workout program.

Body Building Basics

People over 50 should strength-train all major muscle groups at least two to four times per week to gain muscle.

American College of Sports Medicine
  • Muscle actions: concentric, eccentric, and isometric. Good programs include all actions.
  • Compound vs. isolation movements: Compound or multi-joint exercises provide more bang for the buck in terms of activating multiple muscles at the same time. As you get older and do not have a lot of time to spend in the gym and are more prone to injury your exercise program should prioritize the compound movements for maximum efficiency.
  • Exercise order: More demanding multi-joint exercises should be performed before less demanding exercises, and isolation exercises. This way the energy demands on your body are prioritized for maximum results.
  • Proper # of Sets: 3-4 sets per exercise is deemed best by experts to not overtrain.
  • Rest between exercise sets: depends on the periodization emphasis (covered in more detail in 006 Workout Advanced post). The general guidance is to rest enough to allow for maximum effort in the next set.
  • Rest between workouts: 24 to 48 hours rest between workouts. You start to lose gains if you rest 3 days or more.
  • Do NOT train to failure - Research indicates that training to failure adds a lot of fatigue for minimal extra muscle stimulation, which then impacts the effectiveness of the rest of your workout. It is more harmful as the last reps have poor technique and risks injury. Keep in mind though that a slow rep where you fight through is not poor technique but rather "grinding" through a rep which aids hypertrophy.

Why I took a Hybrid Weekly Workout Approach

There are so many approaches to take in working out with varied guidance including:

  • People over 50 years old should just do whole body exercises and do not perform isolation exercises and to rest more (48 hrs for full recovery).
  • Another source indicated a two days workout performing body part splits and then taking one day off is best.

My hybrid plan incorporates elements from different approaches and works for me to balance things out. I find that it is difficult to work out 5 days straight so there often are additional rest days that I throw in. This is fine as I’m in this fitness journey for the long term and not just for short term gains.

Basically the Hybrid Weekly approach I take has full body workouts on Mon & Fri. With body part splits during the week. I put Legs in the middle of the week on purpose to give my other body parts a good rest period before hitting them on Friday.

Hybrid Weekly Approach

Whole body days (Power Circuits 2x a week) + Split body part days = exercising each body part 3 times a week. The initial inspiration for this approach was taken from the Daniel Craig workout that he used to prepare for the James Bond movies.

  • Full Body Circuit days = 3 sets of each exercise but done as a series. First exercise, second exercise
  • Split body part days = 4 sets per exercise, Do all 4 sets then move to next exercise
  • Reps - Controlled and perfect form reps. My goal is more fast twitch so do not do my reps slowly but rather explode and then slowly lower. 1:2 ratio. 

Why I like this approach is that it seems to fit in with all the overall guidance to hit each body part 3 times a week and is a hybrid of the full body approach (which to me would get boring if I did the same thing every workout day) and split body approaches (which pair up alternating/opposing muscle groups when possible) and also throw in some isolation moves.

Warm-up

  • General guidance for your warm up is 10 minutes but really has to be what works for you and is effective.
  • The goal of your warm-up is to get the heart rate up and blood pumping. Typically I run in place for a minute or two and do jumping jacks or dance around, get excited and ready for the workout.
  • Dynamic stretch of the body parts that will be the focus of the workout
  • If full body session then overall dynamic movement to warm up the joints and muscles
  • Before the first exercise practice the movement with no weight or minimal weight
  • Review the best practices of body position and movement for the excercise

Recovery

  • Days off are to be recovery but not inactivity (light cardio recommended & stretching)
  • I’m learning more and more that it really depends on what my body is telling me
  • If I trained too hard my body definitely lets me know
  • If you are sick or cannot train due to some other life circumstance it is not a huge deal so do not beat yourself up. Remember this is a life long fitness journey and is not a short term pursuit for short term gains.

Stretching

  • Stretching is important to reduce chance of injury and to retain a full range of movement as you age.
  • Dynamic stretching before lifting to limber and prepare your muscles for exercise and get your range of motion.
  • Static stretching after lifting as it lengthens your muscles and ligaments and starts to get the lactic acid out. There is research that indicates that static stretching is actually not a good idea before a workout as it does not reduce the chance of injury and that elongating the muscle before you workout actually makes it harder for you to activate your muscles thoroughly during exercise and reduces your level of performance.
    • When doing static stretching the goals is to stretch 60 seconds total for each stretch. Doesn’t matter if 6 - 10 second stretches at a time just needs to add up to 60 seconds.

Fundamental Principles

High-intensity interval training (HIIT) Cardio - For my training goals I focus more on High-intensity interval training (HIIT) vs. Steady-state training. Ideally if you can do your cardio in the morning before eating. When I do my workouts I use weights but limit the amount of rest so I get a cardio benefit from my workout.

Substitute/change up exercises - If you do not have the right equipment or have an injury that prevents you from doing a particular movement substitute/change up your exercises. It is also good to keep your body guessing and to activate the muscles in a new and challenging way so perform a variety of movements. Also consider that every person is different and some movements just are really uncomfortable so find the right exercises that work for you that you can perform with good form and target the muscles you are trying to engage.

Measure progress - body weight weekly, body measurements and pictures on a monthly basis. I’ve been doing this fairly diligently. It is motivating as the mirror doesn’t lie.

Keep Consistent & be patient - Stick with it and you will see gradual results. Do not be discouraged if the gains or losses are not progressing as fast as you would want. Persistence and patience will be rewarded.

I find it really helps to have music when I workout! What do you listen to when you workout?

item.title: 006 Workout Advanced
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
After you have determined your fitness goal (covered in the post - What's your fitness goal?) and understand workout basics (covered in the post - 006 Workout Basics) now it's time to move on to advanced topics which I hope will aid the fine tuning of your personal workout program.

Performance Over Aesthetic

If you have amazing athletic performance, your aesthetic looks great because of performance. We never train for aesthetic, we train for athleticism.

Simon Waterson, Movie Health & Fitness Advisor

Simon Waterson trains actors to be ready for their demanding roles. Most notably Waterson trained Daniel Craig for his James Bond movies. Waterson trains his clients like an athlete and puts performance over looks. When training an actor he focuses on the movements that are relevant to the movie. The looks are the after product. The overall focus is on being healthy, and being able to make it through the production. Speed, agility, and recovery were emphasized for the James Bond movies. Simon tries to replicate the movements in the gym, then takes them to the stunt room, then to the stage. Physical & mental fatigue are challenges for actors who have to deal with grueling shooting schedules of 16 hour+ days.

Diet guidance from Waterson focuses on what will make people feel happy/comfortable. A little more plant based. He doesn’t cut out food groups. Waterson's maxims are good gut health = great absorption and he focuses on anti-inflammatory foods and foods that provide great energy. His diet programs are never about deprivation.

Progressive Overload

There are a few key terms and concepts that are critical to a deeper understanding of how to train your body. Progressive overload is defined as:

  • A bodybuilding principle that involves continually increasing the demands on the musculoskeletal system to continually make gains in muscle size, strength, and endurance.

To get bigger and stronger you have to continually make your muscles work harder than they are used to. Not just more weight but can be more reps or shorter rest.

    Methods to achieve Progressive Overload:

  • Lifting the same load for increased distance (range of motion)
  • Lifting the same load and volume with better form, more control, and less effort (efficiency)
  • Lifting the same load for more reps (volume)
  • Lifting heavier loads (intensity of load)
  • Lifting the same load and volume with less rest time in between sets (density)
  • Lifting a load with more speed and acceleration (intensity of effort)
  • Doing more work in the same amount of time (density)
  • Doing the same work in less amount of time (density)
  • Doing more sets with the same load and reps (volume)
  • Lifting the same load and volume more often throughout the week (frequency)
  • Doing the same work while losing body mass (increased relative volume)
  • Lifting the same load and volume and then extending the set past technical failure with forced reps, negatives, drop sets, static holds, rest pause, partial reps, or post-exhaustion (intensity of effort)

Periodization

When it is time to change up your workout regimen try out periodization. Periodization is defined as:

  • The gradual cycling of specificity, intensity, and volume of training to achieve peak levels of strength. (Training Volume: Is your total workload per exercise, session, and week. Simple equation: Sets x Reps x Load)

Periodization is a helpful strategy for organizing your long-term training plan to cylce different levels of intensity from week to week to keep your body guessing.

Training Volume Schemes for Targeted Goals

Simple Method To Determine your 1RM

  • In order to use the training volume schemes in the above table you first have to determine your one repetition maximum or 1RM. This is the maximum weight per exercise that you can lift for one repetition. It is important to know this as you can then determine the amount of weight you need to lift to hit your desired intensity/repetition to hit your training volume emphasis.
  • It is dangerous to do this and can lead to injury so often people use the following equation/ratios to help determine the right number of repetitions at what weight is appropriate.
    • Your 5RM is roughly equivalent to 85-87.5% of your 1RM
    • Your 3RM to 87.5-90%
    • Your 2RM to 90-92.5%

Supplements

There are a lot of different positions and opinions about whether to take supplements or not. A good friend of mine is a personal trainer and she advocates taking daily supplements. Other experts say this is good to bring into your mix after you have your diet and exercise program nailed.

General guidance:

  • Multi-vitamin - daily
  • Protein powder
    • Whey (fast absorption) - Post workout within 30 minutes
    • Casein (slow absorption) - Before bed
    • If you have allergies or prefer there are plant based options as well
  • BCAAs
  • Glutamine
  • Fish oil
  • Creatine
    • Have to take daily to build up in your system
    • General guidance to take 5g post workout

Different Tools & Techniques

Resistance bands vs. free weights. With free weights the initial part of a movement is difficult and then once you get it moving and it is at the top of the movement it typically doesn't provide much resistance or workout. With resistance bands it actually gets harder the more you stretch the band. It is not meant to completely replace free weights but rather is a good way to vary your workouts. A friend of mine that uses bands regularly finds that it helps to get at the deeper muscle layer and he incorporates repetitions with the bands in between free weight exercises.

Blood Flow Restriction (BFR) training. This is an advanced technique of restricting the blood flow to a body part like your arms or legs to put more stress on your muscles. I have purchased bands and incorporate them during my deload week. I have found a lot of muscle soreness the day following so it seems to work great. BFR training can also be used as a finishing move. Guidance is that it works more for isolation exercises. If you are interested in learning more I found this is a good resource: Your Complete Guide To Blood Flow Restriction Training!

Foam Roller research seems to indicate that doing this prior to workout on areas that are sore stimulates circulation and reduces the pain. Doing the foam roller after is also advised to aid the lactic acid being worked out of the muscles and aids in speeding recovery.

Professional Guidance

  • It is great to get professional guidance and input and I have found it to be invaluable. I shared my goals and workout plan with a friend of mine that is a certified personal trainer.
    • She liked the exercises that I had (in particular that I had the core of squats, deadlift, and bench).
    • She recommended to not focus on Muscular endurance as I had been but rather to achieve my fitness goals to try Periodization. For me this meant to not focus on Muscular Endurance but rather build a program which cycled through the following phases: Strength --> Power --> Deload
  • After incorporating periodization into my routine I had another conversation with my Certified Personal Trainer friend sharing my top two goals which are shared below along with her excellent guidance:
    • Goal #1 Reduce Body fat to 10%
      • Cut calories down to 1,600-1,800/day
      • Hit my macros, in particular must hit my protein goals daily (at least 30g of protein per meal)
    • Goal #2 Increase body dimensions in areas to be proportional
      • Add calories to build at 2,000-2,200/day. And not get to over 15% body fat in the building phase.
      • Have to improve strength and lift more weight to see the improvements I’m looking for in terms of growth
      • Do not remove my lower body workout exercises but to emphasize growth in a particular body part I would need to add more targeted exercises for that area of the body. Can superset or do opposing muscle (push/pull) workout to put more demand on that particular area of the body.
    • Additionally I shared with her that I want to be more flexible and she shared some tips on a stretching routine to help target the areas where I needed the most work.

Intensity - Dedication/Discipline/Design - Honesty

item.title: Food for thought
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
I have been and continue to be a stubborn and slow learner when it comes to seeing life informed by God’s truth and perspective, and having it shape my thinking and behavior. The following devotional is one that I first shared at a Bible Study group that my family was a member of where our motto was "You don't have to be hungry to eat". But that is a story for another time...

When I was 11 years old

My mom had a couple of friends that she had known for many years come over to our house in Mission Viejo, California for a fancy dinner. My mom's friends were both in the broadcast industry and lived in Beverly Hills, California, the lady was a beautiful Japanese television news anchor and her husband was a talent agent that had various celebrities that he managed.

My mom had prepared an elaborate steak dinner with all the fixins. We had the best china laid out for our distinguished guests. I was excited about the food and meeting these important people.

When we sat down to dinner I immediately chanted that I wanted the biggest piece of steak. I was hungry and only thought of myself and my desire. I had no clue about those around me and didn’t really care about them. My dad humored me and I remember the people at the table smiling, which I’m not sure how I interpreted it then as I didn’t really care, but at least I thought I was amusing them. They were probably thinking what a spoiled brat I was and smiling.

I got the biggest steak on my plate with all the fixings. I am hungry and ready to eat. Come on! So others get their food and we all start to dig in. I tried to cut my steak with my fork and knife. Unfortunately I didn’t understand that if you push down hard on the front of your plate that is towards you to cut a steak, it tips your plate over.

My very first attempt to cut the steak landed the entire plate of food in my lap. The beautiful steak, along with all the fixings were now squarely in my lap. Boy was I embarrassed! Again not thinking of others but really just focusing on me. Thinking of how dumb I looked and how the food was now ruined, my clothes dirty. I don’t think I realized how embarrassing that must have been for my parents. But the evening went on and was pleasant despite my incident.

Fast forward to now

Where I am at now in my walk I believe that I at least have the ability to see how my actions might impact others. How they might honor or dishonor the Lord. I combat my childish impulses to gluttony, selfishness and try to at least follow some rules of common courtesy and etiquette. Offering others the first choice of the food for example. Praying out loud to thank the Lord for the meal and ask for His blessing. I have also learned a bit more about physics and gravity and the techniques to keeping my meal on my plate and successfully navigating it into my mouth without mishap.

But seriously I only used this story of the steak incident to illustrate just how small of a step I have taken over all these years to think first about God’s teaching and behave in a manner that honors Him and His commandments.

Honest self reflection

As I look at my life, too often it is characterized by the following characteristics:

  • How much I just think about me and my need for instant gratification
  • How I look at ways that I can avoid pain and maximize pleasure
  • How I lust after and place value in things and fun events versus putting my very best effort to align to God’s will for eternal benefit
  • How I often do not prioritize relationships and in sharing the truth with the lost
  • How I spend too much time in diversion and fun, instead of seeing the urgent need and suffering of those around me and doing something about it

My desire is to not be so focused on myself and my immediate needs and desires. I wish to truly serve those in my family, church, and community. I want the motivation behind these action to not be to seek man's esteem or for how it can benefit me but rather to faithfully serve and obey the Lord. It really has been hard for me to have the right perspective on things. God’s perfect perspective. God’s amazing example in the life here and in His everlasting ministry. How He had and has the power to do whatever He wanted/wants and chose to humble himself to be a human to show us the way. To show us His true nature and  be an example of it. To continue to reveal to us the eternal truth that from His perspective has always been and always will be. I think about how patient He has been, how loving, how faithful.

I am a work in progress

A verse that really struck me recently in my bible reading is as follows:

Therefore, since we have so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, let us also lay aside every encumbrance, and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us, fixing our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

Hebrews 12:1-2

I always had a very simplistic view of this verse. I would simply think that Jesus was really looking forward to getting back to heaven and be done with the very very painful task that He had set before Him.

I think that I have a bit more insight now about the depth of meaning in that verse when I try with my feeble brain to understand it from God’s perspective. How everything He did and continues to do is reflective of His perfect will and character. How He loves His bride which is the Church which is made up of believers. How He planned and purposed to do everything to bring His Father glory.

Questions for reflection

  • Do I have that "joy set before me" perspective on my tasks and chores in life, in my duties as a father, husband, employee, or ministry servant?
  • Do I really even understand what kind of character our Lord has to do what He did and continues to do, and what is yet to come?
  • Do I really live my life with that perspective of His sacrifice?  Of the perspective of finally meeting the Lord face to face and having to give an account?
  • Do I have a fear, an awe at all of Him that has the power to save or cast people into hell forever?
  • Do I live my life in glad obedience to the King of Kings? Or am I more concerned about myself and how others might think of me if I tell them about my hope and joy or even simply ask them to come to church or read the bible.

Just some food for thought and reflection. Steak anyone?

After taking a crazy career path that no one would have ever planned for or imagined (more details in the post entitled "Living the dream") I am now in the entertainment industry and have been working at a movie studio for 10 years now.

This post explores how I continue to live out my faith in Hollywood one day at a time. The story begins with taking a heart check.

Is the entertainment industry for you?

Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the heart.

Proverbs 21:2

Before setting out to pursue a career in the entertainment industry I strongly suggest that you do a heart check on your attitude and motivations. Before I became a Christian and follower of Jesus Christ this was simple. I wanted fortune and glory and the praise and adoration of people. However as a Christian I check my motivations daily to see if they are to honor God or self seeking.

You have to ask yourself is a career in entertainment for you. This applies to any vocation you pursue. There are numerous practical implications as well including where you would work and how it would impact your family and loved ones.

I focused my job search in the entertainment industry primarily at animation studios as they were for the most part family oriented entertainment companies that produce PG or G rated films and shows.

Spiritual Discipline

Having spiritual discipline isn't just applicable to your work but to everything you do in your life. The following is a list of a few areas that are applicable to living out your faith at your work:

  • Guard your tongue and be in the word daily
  • The Lord is your boss so pursue excellence
  • How you live is your testimony before a watching world
  • Be in a discipleship relationship where you have an accountability partner
  • Be a part of a local Church body and serve
  • Be in a small bible study group
  • Preach the gospel to yourself daily

Spiritual Maturity

Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil.

Ephesians 6:11

The process of maturing spiritually is a gradual one over time. Some of the areas that have been particularly challenging during my career have been:

Balancing priorities

  • Family
  • Church
  • Career

Managing stress

  • Saying No
  • Turn off your work
  • Health and fitness

I have come a long way in being able to better balance my priorities and manage stress in my life. However I'm definitely a work in progress and have to remain diligent in this.

item.title: Pursue your Dream Job
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
Whether you are applying for your first job, or making a career transition it can be a daunting proposition. Here are some job hunting strategies that I have successfully used and I hope will aid you in the pursuit of your dream job.

Step 1 - Personal Assessment & Goal Setting

  • Personal Assessment
    • Honestly assess your skills, education, experience and interests
    • Take free career tests to see what types of work fit your personality best
      • Monster.com: Best free career assessment tools
    • Get feedback from your friends and family on what your strengths and talents are
  • Set Goals
    • Pray that the Lord will give you wisdom and discernment about your job hunt and how it will honor and bring Him glory
    • What is your dream job and how can you take steps to get there?
    • Does the job you want have education/certification prerequisites?
    • For me I was in the tech industry and wanted to go back to my High School dream of working in the entertainment industry
    • Set short (in the next year), mid (2-3 years), and long term goals (5+ years)
    • My short term goal was to jump industries from tech to entertainment tech and then explore new opportunities as they arise to keep incrementally working towards my dream job
    • My mid term goal was then to then take my experience in entertainment tech to get to the company I wanted to work for
    • My long term goal was then within the company I wanted to work for to then have the job function/role I wanted to have
    • Some may be able to go straight into the job and company that they want to work for right away, others may have to take a longer journey of getting the education and experience they need to get to where they want to be.

Step 2 - Industry Research

  • Collect a list of all the major players in the industry you are interested in, where they are located, how they are doing financially and if they are hiring
  • For me I wanted to work in the entertainment industry in a solid company that had a good track record and seemed to be an industry leader with good future growth opportunities
  • Also a key criteria for me was location as my wife and I wanted to move to Southern California where we grew up
  • Identify what the jobs/roles you are interested in and what they make
    • There are job salary tools that will help you know what particular job roles make in a given region

Step 3 - Network & Apply to Jobs

The next step is to prepare your resume, cover letter, and update your LinkedIn profile. Never overstate your qualifications as it will come back and hurt you.

  • Networking
    • Reach out to recruiters on LinkedIn at the companies you are interested in joining
      • It is their job to network and connect with people that might be good fits for the companies they represent
    • Connect with professionals who are in the industry and in the companies you are interested in joining
      • Ask them questions like:
        • How they like working there
        • How they got hired
        • To please connect you with the right person in their company to help guide and provide insights on how you can start a career with their company
        • How should you prepare and position yourself for success
        • Are you a good fit for any current open positions?
  • Apply to jobs & track
    • Create a spreadsheet and track all of the careers/job sites of the companies you are interested in
    • For each company you will most likely have to create an online account with your resume
    • You can set up job searches that email you when new opportunities come up
      • However I just checked the sites regularly to not miss any new job postings
    • For each job you apply to keep a copy of the job description as it will come in handy

Once you start applying to specific positions then write your recruiters and professionals that you networked with to let them know the specific job postings you applied to and ask them if they could give you any guidance or insight into these positions and see if you would be a good fit.

It often takes months if not a full year before you hear back from some companies. In my last job move it took three months of searching and applying. I have a friend where she didn't hear from a company for a full year.

Step 4 - Interviewing & Negotiating

You finally got a response on your application and they want to talk with you!

  • Interviewing Prep
    • Often your first interview will be a phone interview with the recruiter
    • Be ready for the interview by re-reading the job posting for the position you applied for
    • Make sure that you can clearly articulate how your skills and experiences line up with the job description
    • Practice answering tough interview questions with your friends and family
    • When I interview I keep a pad of paper ready to write down the questions they ask me and jot down the key points I want to make when answering
    • Do not be afraid of asking clarifying questions if the question is not clear to you
      • Be sure you understand the question and then give your succinct and well thought out answer
    • Be prepared with questions that you might have
  • Interviewing Tips
    • Be attentive and show your enthusiasm
    • For me I am very animated and have learned that I need to sometimes sit on my hands so that I am not just waving them around like crazy which is a major distraction
    • Speak clearly, with confidence, and make eye contact
    • Remember that this is a two way conversation where they are trying to figure out if you would be a good fit for their company
      • You should be doing the same to see if it is a good fit for you
    • If they do ask you about your salary requirements you must be ready with an honest answer and if challenged be able to back it up with facts based on your research
      • This typically happens a bit later in the process when they like you and want to make an offer
    • For video conference call interviews or in person interviews be sure to dress nicely and be punctual

You made it through all your interviews and now they are making their offer to you for the position!

  • Negotiating Tips
    • What I have found is that some companies will try to low ball you in terms of the salary
    • This is where you must be ready and have done your research and find out what these positions are being paid in the region
    • It is often the case that negotiating for your pay at the start of your job is the only time this will happen
    • Know your salary requirement and be able to articulate it succinctly and clearly!
    • If the company wants you they will counter offer and try their best to meet your salary requirements

Final Thoughts & Encouragement

Life is a journey where we will face many challenges and setbacks. There will be victories and defeats. You will make mistakes along the way. Learn from them and move on. Do not be afraid to go after your dreams. Pray every step of the way.

Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

1 Thessalonians 5:16-18

In my previous post entitled Psychology of Motivation I shared some insights from Dr. Jordan Peterson about maximizing your motivation.

What is Motivation?

According to the Oxford English Dictionary motivation is a noun that means "a reason or reasons for acting or behaving in a particular way."

Why is it important?

Your reason or reasons for acting or behaving in a particular way impact every area of your life. Every day, moment by moment, from when you wake up in the morning to when you lay down at night, you have to make decisions about what you are going to do with the time you have. Having a proper understanding and mastery of your motivations are essential to achieving life goals, dreams, and aspirations. For a Christian your motivations are incredibly important as everything you think and do is understood by God, and either honors or dishonors Him, or brings Him joy or does not.

Biblical understanding of motivation

In the area of motivation the bible has a great deal to say. To start with God is incredibly interested in our motivations, the why behind what we do. The bible tells us that our motivation should not be for selfish gain or to seek the approval of men but rather our motivation should come from a desire to obey and honor God.

What is motivation?

According to the Oxford English Dictionary motivation is a noun that means "a reason or reasons for acting or behaving in a particular way."

Why is it important?

Your reason or reasons for acting or behaving in a particular way impact every area of your life. Every day, moment by moment, from when you wake up in the morning to when you lay down at night, you have to make decisions about what you are going to do with the time you have. Having a proper understanding and mastery of your motivations are essential to achieving life goals, dreams, and aspirations.

Psychological approach to motivation

I recently watched a thought provoking video from Dr. Jordan B. Peterson that provided interesting insights into achieving maximal motivation. The video clip below is from a class lecture he did where Dr. Peterson was preparing his students to participate in a future authoring exercise. In this exercise he wanted the students to outline their desired future and also the place that they would end up if everything fell apart.

What I took away from Dr. Peterson's video was that in addition to having a voluntary goal that you choose versus having one chosen for you it is helpful to combine that motivation to achieve that goal with wanting to avoid the worst case scenario where you do not achieve the goal.

Dr. Peterson explained that with humans there is an element of fear where people fear that they will not be able to achieve their goal which weakens them. To overcome this weakness Dr. Peterson asserts that you should combine your pull and push motivations to maximize your motivation. The formula for this is shown below:

Pull Motivation + Push Motivation = Maximal Motivation

  • Pull Motivation = the desire to achieve a goal in front of you, your approach systems pulling you forward
  • Push Motivation = the fear of the undesirable outcome behind you, your anxiety chasing you and pushing you forward

I definitely find some helpful and thought provoking concepts from men like Dr. Peterson and others. However there is no better resource for wisdom and truth than the bible. In my next post I will explore what the bible has to say on the topic of motivation.
