item.title: Sleep Ops
item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
Sleep is so important that I wanted to learn more about what I could do to have the best sleep possible. This post shares some of my research about sleep, and how I performed a sleep study to try out different outfits to figure out the best sleepwear that worked for me.

Benefits of Sleep

Sleep allows your body (energy consumption reduction) and mind (brain cell restoration) to recharge. Without enough sleep your brain cannot function properly and impairs your ability to concentrate, think clearly, and to recall memories. Most adults require seven to nine hours of sleep a day. During sleep, your muscles recover, growth hormone is produced, and protein synthesis occurs (if you consumed protein prior to sleep).

Best Practices

With the internet there is so much information out there about sleep and sometimes it is conflicting. Here are some best practices that I have compiled that work for me.

  • Go to bed and get up at the same time every day
  • Right when you get up get sunlight/bright light for 2-10 minutes as it helps set your internal clock
  • Don't oversleep as it may set your body clock to a different cycle
  • Avoid bright lights late at night as it messes up your internal clock
  • Do not look at computer or phone screens late at night
  • Only have sex (in marriage) and sleep in bed - do not do other activities there
  • Be clean (some sources say to take a warm bath) and have clean sheets
  • In particular I change out my pillow case every couple days which helps to limit allergens building up
  • Don't exercise right before bed unless that is the only time you can
  • Avoid alcohol or caffeine at night
  • Avoid taking sleeping pills as they may work temporarily but in the long term will cause disturbed sleep patterns
  • Try having a nice scent in the air before bed
  • Have the temperature around 67 degrees Fahrenheit in the bedroom
  • Some sources suggest having white noise (a small fan running) or soft background music to help you to relax and encourage sleep

Sleep Study Approach/Tactics

My hypothesis prior to setting about with a sleep study was that I could try out different sleep wear and find the one that gave me the most comfortable sleep. In my sleep study I wanted to push my normal sleepwear boundaries and boldly go where I had never gone before. For me that was wearing socks. I have very rarely worn socks when I go to sleep other than when I was in the Army in the field. For some people they have such cold feet that they must wear socks and sweats to bed. But for me I am always warm and get way too hot in bed.

Sleep Journal - Take notes from each night of sleep to figure out how long I sleep, how many times I wake up, how many times I go to pee, etc…

Try Pillow App - There are numerous apps that do this. I tried the sleep monitoring, but did not try the alarm function which is supposed to wake you up at your ideal time.

Try different outfits - Long sleeve pajama set - my current go to configuration. Would like to try out different combinations to see if I sleep better.

Sleepwear Outfit Alternatives

  1. Pajama long sleeve set with socks
  2. Heavier weight long sleeve set
  3. Pajama long sleeve set - current go to configuration
  4. Pajama long sleeve top and boxer shorts
  5. Pajama long sleeve top and briefs
  6. Long sleeve T-shirt pajama bottom
  7. Long sleeve T-shirt and boxer shorts
  8. Long sleeve T-shirt and briefs
  9. Short sleeve shirt and pajama bottoms
  10. Short sleeve shirt and boxers
  11. Short sleeve shirt and briefs
  12. A-type t-shirt and pajama bottoms
  13. A-type t-shirt and boxers
  14. A-type t-shirt and briefs
  15. Just a hat
  16. Just Pajama top
  17. Just Long sleeve T-shirt
  18. Just T-shirt
  19. Just A-type t-shirt
  20. Just pajama bottoms
  21. Just boxers
  22. Just briefs
  23. Just socks
  24. Just gloves
  25. Naked

Determine hot spots

  • Per thermoscans of the human body there are areas of the body that put out a lot of heat
    • Neck
    • Shoulders
    • Back
    • Spine
    • Groin
    • Palms
  • Cool areas of the body per thermal scan
    • Top of head
    • Upper arms
    • Butt
    • Ankles/feet

Test Results - Excerpts

No - Short sleeve T-shirt - boxers - light socks

  • Fell asleep quickly
  • Woke up 2 times
    • Cat one time
  • No sweat
  • Didn’t go pee
  • Arms were cold
  • Would prefer longer sleeve shirt, more comfy underwear, and more comfy socks

OK - Long sleeve T-shirt - briefs, light socks

  • Fell asleep fairly quickly
  • Woke up 3 times
    • Earthquake was one of the times
  • No sweat
  • Did have to go pee
  • Socks used (CK super soft dress ones) were good, underwear was a tiny bit tight (may want a boxer that is more form fitting but not floppy, long sleeve shirt fabric was a bit warm for my taste

Good - Long sleeve T-shirt - boxers, light socks

  • Was hot from eating too much
  • Only used top sheet over my body
  • Had window open to make bedroom cooler
  • Woke up 1 time (cat howling)
  • No sweat
  • Was cold a bit
  • Did not have to go pee
  • Socks are the winner I think and critical for me for a good night sleep.
  • The boxers I used were good. They are not soft but they were not too long and baggy.
  • Shirt I still think could be a softer and more breathing fabric also ¾ length sleeves

No - Pajama top - boxers, no socks

  • Window was open
  • I sweat and woke up 2 times
    • Once to pee
  • Did not feel good
  • Must not forget to wear socks!!

Good - Pajama top, boxers, socks

  • Window was open a bit
  • I woke up 1 time and went pee
  • Then really couldn’t go back to sleep
  • Was very comfortable

Good - Pajama top, boxers, socks

  • Window was open a bit
  • I woke up 2 times and did not go pee
  • First time I woke up my legs were outside the covers and cold but overall I was not cold. I think I was originally too hot or uncomfortable so I took my legs out. My right foot hurt from working out so maybe was a factor
  • Overall it was a comfortable outfit

Key Learnings/Findings

Individual results may vary but this is what I found out that worked best for me.

Socks are a must!! Lightweight, loosely fitting, just over ankle seems best (my Nike workout little socks seem perfect, maybe a tiny bit looser ones would be good, but those work nicely). I never wore socks before and was very skeptical as I do not like anything on my feet. But there actually is a lot of research out there that supports that wearing socks actually helps you sleep.

Warming up your feet and hands can initiate a process called vasodilation (widening of the blood vessels) which can help prepare your brain for sleep.

According to the National Sleep Foundation

Boxer shorts that are comfortable but not too baggy. Doesn’t need the fly opening. Are there boxers that do not have a fly?

Long sleeved pajama top or shirt - pretty close tie between the two. For some reason I like having a collar as that little bit more fabric keeps my comfortable and cozy.

Pima Cotton Fabric - Soft and breathes well this is the go to fabric for me.

Final Thoughts

There are many other options to try out in the future including introducing eye cover, a hat, or gloves into the mix. For me I don't think a hat would work as I would be too hot and it would fall off, gloves maybe, an eye cover probably would fall off as well.

I encourage you to try out your own sleep study and find out what works best for you. For me it was well worth it as I have dialed in a sleeping outfit that is the most comfortable for me.

item.dc:creator: glennkelly006
item.content:encoded:
This post shares what I have learned about why drinking water everyday is important, what happens if you have too much or too little water, what are electrolytes, how much water should you drink, what is the healthiest water to drink, what container should you drink it in, and what the best times are to drink water. At the end of the article I briefly explain what "living water" is from the Bible quote above which is actually even more important than drinking water is for our life!

Why drinking water is important

Around 60% of your body is made up of water and our blood is 90% water. Water is essential for the kidneys and other bodily functions, without drinking water we would become dehydrated and die in a matter of days. Here is a list of 15 benefits of drinking water everyday (from MedicalNewsToday):

  1. Lubricates your joints (cartilage, found in joints and the disks of the spine, contains around 80% water)
  2. Forms saliva and mucus (which helps us digest our food and keeps the mouth, nose, and eyes moist, preventing friction and damage)
  3. Delivers oxygen throughout the body through your blood
  4. Boosts skin health and beauty (with dehydration your skin becomes more vulnerable to skin disorders and premature wrinkling)
  5. Cushions the brain, spinal cord, and sensitive tissues
  6. Regulates body temperature
  7. Your digestive systems depends on it
  8. Flushes body waste
  9. Helps maintain blood pressure
  10. Your airways need it
  11. Makes minerals and nutrients accessible
  12. Prevents kidney damage
  13. Boosts your performance during exercise
  14. Helps with weight loss
  15. Reduces the chance of a hangover from overconsumption of alcohol

Too much water?

Did you know that drinking too much water can actually be harmful to you? When you drink too much water it is called overhydration.

When you drink too much water, you may experience water poisoning, intoxication, or a disruption of brain function. This happens when there's too much water in the cells (including brain cells), causing them to swell. When the cells in the brain swell they cause pressure in the brain.

What Happens When You Drink Too Much Water? - WebMD

Sodium is a crucial element that helps keep the balance of fluids in and out of your body's cells. Sodium is the electrolyte most affected by overhydration that leads to a condition called hyponatremia.

When its [sodium] levels drop due to a high amount of water in the body, fluids get inside the cells. Then the cells swell, putting you at risk of having seizures, going into a coma, or even dying.

What Happens When You Drink Too Much Water? - WebMD

Too little water?

Dehydration happens when your body does not have as much water as it needs. Without enough water, your body cannot function properly. The following diagram shows some warning signs of not drinking enough water:

Depending on how much fluid is missing from your body you can have mild, moderate, or severe dehydration. Dehydration is very serious, to learn more click the image above to take you to the WebMD article "What is Dehydration? What Causes It?"

What are electrolytes?

Electrolytes are minerals that are essential for your body to help regulate your pH levels and muscles, keep you hydrated, and more. Some of the common electrolytes found in the body are in the diagram below:

Each of these minerals shown in the diagram above carry an electric charge when dissolved in the body, giving them their name as an electrolyte.

The amount of water in your body needs to be in balance with your electrolyte levels. Dehydration from diarrhea, sweating, and liver problems can upset that balance. Maintaining an adequate intake of both substances is fundamental to good health.

Healthy Foods High in Electrolytes - WebMD

How much water should I drink?

Unfortunately there is no simple one size fits all answer to this question. We often hear that we should drink at least eight glasses of water a day. Per the U.S. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine the adequate daily fluid intake is:

  • For men: About 15.5 cups (3.7 liters) of fluids a day
  • For women: About 11.5 cups (2.7 liters) of fluids a day

However you might need to modify your total fluid intake based on several factors:

  • Age, gender, weight - Your body needs different amounts of water if you are one year old or a 100 years old, whether you are a man or a woman, or weigh 100 lbs or 250 lbs.
  • Exercise - You need to drink extra water to cover the fluid loss from sweat.
  • Environment - Hot or humid weather can make you sweat and requires additional fluids. Dehydration can also occur at high altitudes.
  • Overall health - If you are ill your body loses fluids when you have a fever, are vomiting or have diarrhea.
  • Pregnancy and breast-feeding - If you are pregnant or breast-feeding you may need additional fluids to stay hydrated.

A couple of indicators that you probably have adequate fluid intake are if:

  1. You rarely feel thirsty
  2. Your urine is colorless or light yellow

Keep in mind that you don't need to rely only on water to meet your fluid needs. What you eat also provides a significant portion. Beverages such as milk, juice and herbal teas are composed of mostly water. Even coffee and soda can contribute to your daily water intake.

What is the healthiest water to drink?

There are so many different types of water. In the table below I have listed the top 10 most common types of water and their pros and cons.

Filtered or mineral drinking water is free from contaminants but still contains a good amount of healthy minerals and electrolytes. Other healthy waters are soda water and infused water, as long as these do not have added sodium, sugars, or sulfates.

All types of water have their pros and cons. For instance, purified water is technically very healthy because it lacks all dangerous contaminants, but it also lacks beneficial minerals. You will need to determine for yourself which type of water is best for you.

Does it matter what you put your water in?

The short answer is Yes! When I was a kid I used to drink water out of the garden hose, which in hindsight was probably not the best idea. Plastic bottles are made using a chemical compound known as polyethylene terephthalate (PET) that acccording to several studies, can contaminate water. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) points out that bisphenol A (BPA), which is used to harden plastic containers and to line metal cans, "can act like estrogen in the body and potentially change the timing of puberty, decrease fertility, increase body fat, and affect the nervous and immune systems." There are a plethora of research articles and web sites that debate this, however the bottom line is the healthier choice is to avoid the risks of drinking from plastic containers.

Best timing to drink water

Living Water

The phrase "living water" is in two instances in the Bible. In John 4:10 where Jesus was speaking with the Samaritan woman at the well, "Jesus answered and said to her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give Me a drink,’ you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.” And from John 7:38 quoted at the beginning of this post. Living Water is referring to the Holy Spirit that Jesus gives to those that believe in him as their Savior and Lord who will inherit eternal life. Nothing in life is more important than this.

Final Thoughts & Encouragement

  • If you live in the area or are visiting come worship with us at Oak Hill Bible Church
  • For amazing Bible teaching and resources to apply biblical discernment to all you do subscribe to the Oak Hill Bible Church YouTube channel.

The name's Kelly, Glenn Kelly

I’m 006, an Army Airborne Ranger veteran and DreamWorker blessed to have led projects at Apple, Microsoft, World Vision, and DreamWorks. With a BA in Film & Television, an MBA, and project management certifications, I’ve woven my love for movies and global leadership into stories of resilience, purpose, and faith in Christ.

As a husband, father of two, and Deacon at Oak Hill Bible Church in Stevenson Ranch, California, I humbly share personal stories through my blog posts and BONDFIRE podcast (in development) to ignite your passion for living boldly in Christ with biblical wisdom, workout strategies, career tips, and fun movie tributes.
